On a privately owned forum, the owners have the full right to dictate who is allowed to post and to establish any limits they might desire on what they may post. So it's not really a matter of whether or not this or that person "deserves" "free speech".

In the first place, their speech is not necessarily free - it may rightly be constrained in whatever manner the owners of the forum might decree. This is a thing that all too many people don't grasp about "free speech." You have no guarantee of "free speech" broadly. You (presuming you're a citizen of a nation that recognizes a right to free speech) are protected from having your speech constrained by your government. That's it. There's no protection of free speech when you're on someone else's private property. It's their property and they get to set the rules and that's just the way it is.

So really, there can be no broad notion of whether or not they "deserve" it (much less any sort of objective standard by which to measure that). It's entirely and completely up to the owners, and they can make their judgments based on whatever criteria they might prefer.

And I know this might be difficult for some to accept, but you, unless you're one of the aforementioned owners, have absolutely no say in the matter. If the owners wish to recognize some notion of "free speech," then that's what they'll do. If they don't, then they won't. It's their property and they get to decide. Since it's not your property, the only decision you get to make is whether or not to avail yourself of the service they provide on their property.
